To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NsrR1, an NtcA regulated sRNA, controls nblA mRNA stability, and that NblA, the protein encoded by nblA, is a target of NsrR.
we identified an sRNA that is under the control of Ntc A and that regulates nblA expression in the nitrogen starved state of Nostoc sp. PCC 712 0.
NsrR1, an NtcA regulated sRNA in the filamentous cyanobacterium, Nostoc sp PCC 71200, contributes to the regulation of nblA expression, by interacting with the 5′ untranslated region of nblA mRNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new regulatory mechanism of gene expression in cyanobacteria, that may be of interest for other prokaryotes.
the identification of an NtcA-controlled sRNA that is involved in the regulation of the expression of nblAp, encoding an adaptor protein of phycobilisomes.
a new regulatory network involving a transcription factor, an sRNA and a target gene, that is involved in the regulation of phycobilisomes in response to nitrogen availability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NtcA is a transcriptional regulator of NsrR, which is in turn a post-transcriptional regulator of nblA.
NsrR1 contributes to the regulation of nblA by NtcA.
the sRNA NsrR1 is involved in the control of nblA mRNA expression in response to nitrogen starvation in Nostoc PCC7120.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NsrR1 is a post-transcriptional repressor of the NtcA regulon.
the transcription factor NtcA, that controls the expression of the sRNA NsrR1, regulates the expression of nbl A by a direct interaction between Nsr R1 and the 3′-end of the 5′UTR of nblA mRNA.
NsrR1 contributes to the regulation of nblA expression in response to nitrogen starvation in Nostoc.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of gene expression in Nostoc is not only controlled by transcription factors, but also by sRNAs.
the interplay between transcription factors and sRNA can lead to complex regulatory networks, where both transcription factors and small RNAs may appear as network nodes.

sRNAs can participate in complex regulatory networks, in which they can act as nodes in a regulatory network, and that the interplay between sRNA, transcription factor, and mRNA can lead to coherent feed-forward loop regulatory circuits.
